content: The regimen consists of one pink active tablet daily for 21 consecutive days, followed by one light-green inert tablet daily for 7 consecutive days. It is crucial to take the tablets at the same time each day. The pill dispenser should be stored in the provided wallet to prevent fading of the tablets. If fading occurs, the pills remain effective and should still be taken as directed. During the First Cycle of Use Before starting Alesse, the possibility of ovulation and conception must be considered. Patients may begin the medication using one of two methods: the Sunday Start or the Day 1 Start. Sunday Start The patient should take the first pink tablet on the first Sunday after menstruation begins. If menstruation starts on a Sunday, the first tablet is taken that same day. One pink tablet is taken daily for 21 days, followed by one light-green tablet daily for 7 days. Withdrawal bleeding typically occurs within 3 days after stopping the pink tablets and may not be complete before starting the next pack. During the first cycle, Alesse should not be relied upon for contraception until 7 consecutive days of pink tablets have been taken. A nonhormonal back-up method, such as condoms or spermicide, must be used during this initial 7-day period. Day 1 Start The patient begins taking Alesse within the first 24 hours of her menstrual cycle (Day 1 of menstruation). One pink tablet is taken daily for 21 days, followed by one light-green tablet daily for 7 days. Withdrawal bleeding typically occurs within 3 days after stopping the pink tablets and may not be complete before starting the next pack. If Alesse is started on Day 1 of the menstrual cycle, no back-up contraception is required. However, if the medication is started later than Day 1, a nonhormonal back-up method must be used for the first 7 days of administration. After the First Cycle of Use Subsequent packs of Alesse should be started the day after the last light-green tablet is taken. The same dosing schedule (21 days of pink tablets followed by 7 days of light-green tablets) should be followed. If the patient starts a new pack later than the proper day, a nonhormonal back-up method must be used until 7 consecutive days of pink tablets have been taken. Switching from Another Hormonal Contraceptive From a 21-day regimen: The patient should wait 7 days after the last tablet of the previous regimen before starting Alesse. Withdrawal bleeding is expected during this interval. No more than 7 days should elapse between regimens. From a 28-day regimen: The patient should start Alesse the day after the last tablet of the previous regimen without any gap. From a progestin-only pill: Alesse should be started the day after the last progestin-only pill. From an implant or injection: Alesse should be started on the day the implant is removed or the day the next injection would be due. In all cases, a nonhormonal back-up method should be used for the first 7 days of Alesse administration. Spotting or Breakthrough Bleeding If spotting or breakthrough bleeding occurs, the patient should continue taking the tablets as scheduled. This type of bleeding is usually temporary and not clinically significant. However, if the bleeding persists or becomes prolonged, the patient should consult her physician. Risk of Pregnancy if Tablets Are Missed The likelihood of ovulation increases with each consecutive day that active pink tablets are missed. If withdrawal bleeding does not occur, pregnancy should be considered. If the patient has not adhered to the prescribed schedule, pregnancy should be evaluated at the time of the first missed period. If the patient has followed the regimen but misses two consecutive periods, pregnancy must be ruled out. The risk of pregnancy increases with each missed active tablet. Use After Pregnancy, Abortion, or Miscarriage Postpartum or after a second-trimester abortion: Alesse may be started no earlier than 28 days postpartum or after a second-trimester abortion due to the increased risk of thromboembolism. A nonhormonal back-up method should be used for the first 7 days of Alesse administration. After a first-trimester abortion or miscarriage: Alesse may be started immediately, and no back-up contraception is required. What to Do If You Miss Pills If You Miss 1 Pink Active Pill Take the missed pill as soon as you remember. Take the next pill at your regular time, even if it means taking two pills in one day. Use a nonhormonal back-up method for the next 7 days if you have sexual intercourse. If You Miss 2 Pink Active Pills in a Row in Week 1 or Week 2 Take two pills on the day you remember and two pills the next day. Then take one pill daily until the pack is finished. Use a nonhormonal back-up method for the next 7 days if you have sexual intercourse. If You Miss 2 Pink Active Pills in a Row in Week 3 Day 1 Starter: Discard the remaining pills in the pack and start a new pack the same day. Sunday Starter: Continue taking one pill daily until Sunday. On Sunday, discard the remaining pills in the pack and start a new pack the same day. You may not have a period this month, but this is expected. If you miss your period for two consecutive months, consult your healthcare provider to rule out pregnancy. Use a nonhormonal back-up method for the next 7 days if you have sexual intercourse. If You Miss 3 or More Pink Active Pills in a Row (During the First 3 Weeks) Day 1 Starter: Discard the remaining pills in the pack and start a new pack the same day. Sunday Starter: Continue taking one pill daily until Sunday. On Sunday, discard the remaining pills in the pack and start a new pack the same day. You may not have a period this month, but this is expected. If you miss your period for two consecutive months, consult your healthcare provider to rule out pregnancy. Use a nonhormonal back-up method for the next 7 days if you have sexual intercourse. If You Forget Any of the 7 Light-Green Reminder Pills in Week 4 Discard the missed pills and continue taking one pill daily until the pack is empty. No back-up contraception is needed if you start your next pack on time.
